_note: Week of Nov. 16 capsules, written from the frozen fact sheet in 2026-11-16.json.
wright-state:
There are fast starts, and then there is what Wright State did last week, which was to leave Dayton twice and come home twice with the other team's lunch money. On Tuesday the Raiders won at Toledo, 76-68, against a team that sits third in the MAC's own rankings this week. On Friday they won at Samford, 90-66, by 24, in Alabama, in the season's second week. The Raiders are 4-0, and the Bricks Index has noticed in the loudest way it knows how.

Recent form puts Wright State at plus-12.5 points a game against an average Division I team, and the two road wins add another 2.2, more road credit than any team in the four leagues we rank. The total is plus-14.7. That is first in the Horizon by nearly fourteen points, and it is the highest index in the MAC, the Horizon, the ASUN or the Mountain West this week. It is not a close race. It is a parade.

The parade has three drum majors. Andrea Holden, a junior guard, is averaging 14.5 points and 8.5 rebounds, a guard collecting rebounds at a forward's rate, as if the paint were simply another place he likes to be. Kellen Pickett, a sophomore forward, adds 14.2 points, seven rebounds and 2.8 assists. Dominic Pangonis, a junior guard, is at 13.0.

Nobody is averaging twenty. Nobody has to. A team whose three leading scorers are separated by a point and a half is a team that is very hard to scheme against, because there is no one person to take away.

The week offers a pause. Malone, a non-Division I opponent, visits the Nutter Center on Wednesday, and that is the whole card. It will not move the number much in either direction.

Which is fine. Wright State spent last week making a statement on the road. This week, it gets to stay home and let everyone else read it.
youngstown-state:
Youngstown State is No. 2 in the Horizon with a recent form below average, and the explanation fits on one line of the road ledger: St. Bonaventure, 79-71, Nov. 2. That win, in western New York, against a team the season-long model rates well, is worth 1.6 points a game, the largest single road win in the conference this week. Recent form is minus-0.6. The total, plus-0.9, is enough for second in a league that is still sorting itself out behind Wright State.

The week split. On Tuesday the Penguins went to Central Michigan and lost 91-78, the kind of night when a road team finds out how long forty minutes can be. On Saturday they came home and beat Marshall 74-71, a three-point win over a Sun Belt team.

That is a 2-2 record with real names on it, and the Index tends to reward that kind of schedule over time even when it does not show up in the win column.

Linus Holmstrom, a junior guard, leads the scoring at 14.3 points a game over three appearances. Kelvin Amoako, a senior center, adds 11.0 points and 7.5 rebounds, the presence in the middle that lets everyone else take chances on the perimeter. Jaiden Haynes, a sophomore guard, is at 10.8 points and 2.8 assists.

The week is a dare. On Wednesday the Penguins go to Cincinnati, a Big 12 program on its own floor, the sort of road game the formula prices as generously as any. On Sunday William & Mary visits.

The Cincinnati game is the one that will tell the story. A loss there is expected and costs little. A win would put Youngstown State in a conversation it has not been invited to yet. The Penguins have already shown they will go anywhere. Now they get to show what they do when they arrive.
green-bay:
Green Bay is 3-2, third in the Horizon, and holding its place on the strength of one trip across the state line into Minnesota. The Phoenix won at St. Thomas on Nov. 8, 76-67, and the win is still worth 1.0 point a game on the road ledger more than a week later. Recent form is minus-2.1. The total is minus-1.2, and in a league where only two teams are above zero, that is good enough for third.

The week had both kinds of evening. On Tuesday the Phoenix went to Northern Iowa and lost 89-76, the kind of game that a team in November uses as a measuring stick and then quietly puts away. On Friday they came home and beat Viterbo, a non-Division I opponent, 66-46.

The roster is built on guards. Orlando Lovejoy, a senior, leads at 13.0 points and 2.8 assists. Ne'quan Brown, a junior, adds 12.0 points and five rebounds. Marcus Hall, a senior forward, is at 10.6. Three players in double figures, none above thirteen: it is a team that wins by committee and loses the same way, which at least has the virtue of honesty.

The week takes the Phoenix a long way from Lake Michigan. On Tuesday they play at West Florida in Pensacola. On Friday they play at Florida State in Tallahassee. Two road games in four days in a state where it is not snowing, which may be the most pleasant thing that happens to this team all winter.

The Florida State game is the big one, the kind of road opponent the Index pays handsomely for. The West Florida game is the one that has to be won, because the formula does not forgive a team for losing the game it was supposed to take. Green Bay will come home with a sunburn either way. The ranking will depend on what else it brings back.
milwaukee:
Milwaukee is 2-3 and fourth in the Horizon, and if there is a theme to the Panthers' season so far, it is that they keep getting on planes. On Wednesday they won at Indiana State, 82-73, a nine-point road win in the Missouri Valley that is worth 0.7 points a game on the ledger. On Friday they went to TCU and lost 76-64, against a Big 12 team on its own floor. Recent form is minus-2.0. The total is minus-1.3.

That is a team that has played a hard early schedule and come through it bruised but upright, which in November is roughly what a coach hopes for.

The most interesting name on the roster is a freshman. Amare Hereford, a guard, is averaging 14.0 points, 4.0 rebounds and 5.0 assists over five games, leading the team in scoring and in setting up others at an age when most players are still learning the playbook. There is a particular kind of first-year guard who arrives already sure the ball belongs in his hands, and the early numbers suggest Hereford is one of them.

Behind him the scoring is spread thin. Tre Norman, a senior guard, is at 9.0 points and 4.4 rebounds. Chandler Jackson, a senior forward, is also at 9.0. It is a roster that leans on its freshman more than most teams would like, and it is worth watching whether the seniors can take some of the weight off him as the season goes on.

The week brings one game, at home: St. Thomas on Saturday, a team Green Bay already beat on the road. It will not add road credit, but it is a winnable game in front of the home crowd, and after a week that ended in Fort Worth, a winnable game at home sounds about right.

Hereford will have the ball. The question is who he finds when he looks up.
northern-illinois:
Northern Illinois has won three straight and has collected two road wins in the process, which makes the Huskies' minus-3.3 index a little hard to explain until you look at what came before. The road wins are real: 81-76 at Dayton on Nov. 7, the kind of result that gets a program noticed in November, and 72-64 at Bellarmine on Saturday. Together they are worth 1.2 points a game. Recent form, still carrying the weight of two early losses, is minus-4.5. The total is fifth in the Horizon.

The home win in between came Wednesday, 82-43 over Clarke, a non-Division I opponent, the sort of game that is mostly about getting the bench some minutes.

The backcourt runs the team. Max Weisbrod, a senior guard, is averaging 15.6 points and 6.8 assists, the line of a point guard who knows exactly where everyone is supposed to be and gets them the ball when they get there. David Douglas Jr., another senior guard, adds 14.8 points and 6.4 rebounds, a guard who crashes the glass as if he has a personal grudge against it. Brayden Gross, a sophomore forward, is at 8.4 points and seven rebounds.

Two senior guards carrying the scoring and the playmaking is the sort of thing that tends to hold up over a long season, when the games get closer and the possessions matter more.

The week is two road games, and both of them matter. Wednesday the Huskies go to Marquette, a Big East team on its own floor, the kind of opponent the Index pays very well for. Saturday they go to Bowling Green, an old MAC neighbor unbeaten so far this season.

Northern Illinois has shown it will win in other people's buildings. This week offers two more buildings. The formula is waiting to see what the Huskies take from them.
purdue-fort-wayne:
Purdue Fort Wayne is 2-2 and sixth in the Horizon, and the week told you about both halves of the team. On Thursday the Mastodons hosted Western Michigan and lost 81-59, a home loss by 22 that the model took at full weight. On Sunday they went to Eastern Illinois and won 86-74, a twelve-point road win that put 0.4 points a game on the ledger. Recent form is minus-6.4. The total is minus-6.0.

Those two results, three days apart, are the sort of thing that makes November so hard to read. A team that loses by 22 at home and wins by twelve on the road is either still finding itself or is two different teams depending on the night, and four games is not enough to know.

The scoring leans on two seniors. Anthony Isaac Jr., a forward, leads at 13.8 points a game. DeAndre Craig Jr., a guard, adds 11.0 points, 4.2 rebounds and 3.0 assists, the kind of all-around line that a team needs from its veterans. Carl Thompson III, a freshman guard, is at 10.7 in three games, a young player already trusted to score.

What the Mastodons need is the version of themselves that showed up in Charleston, the one that scored 86 and won by twelve in a road gym. That version would move up this ranking quickly.

The week offers a chance to find it. On Wednesday Fort Wayne goes to Bradley, a Missouri Valley program with a long basketball memory, a real road test and a chance at real road credit. On Saturday Calumet St. Joseph, a non-Division I opponent, comes to town.

The Bradley game is the one that matters. A win in Peoria would say the Eastern Illinois game was not a fluke. A loss would say the jury is still out. Either way, the Mastodons will know a little more about who they are by Sunday.
oakland:
Oakland is 1-5, and before anyone says anything about that record, consider last week alone. The Golden Grizzlies played at Alabama on Monday and lost 109-68, then flew to Boise State on Wednesday and lost 111-79. That is a travel schedule no one would choose for the fun of it.

Then on Saturday they came home and beat Northern Iowa, 80-76. That is the same Northern Iowa that beat Green Bay by thirteen on Tuesday. It was Oakland's first win of the season, and it was a good one.

The Bricks Index has Oakland at minus-6.5 points a game, all recent form and no road credit, seventh in the Horizon. That number was built mostly in hostile gyms, and it will not take much to move it.

The scoring has two pillars. Nassim Mashhour, a junior guard, is averaging 18.3 points over six games. Chris Fields Jr., a senior forward, is averaging 18.0 points and 10.8 rebounds, a double-double average sustained through a brutal early schedule, which is a fact worth sitting with. Ryder Bradley, a sophomore guard, adds 7.3.

Fields and Mashhour together account for more than 36 points a night. On a team that has been playing uphill for two weeks, that is not just production. It is a refusal to be overwhelmed.

The tour is not over. On Wednesday Oakland plays at Arizona State. On Friday it plays at Purdue. Two more buildings where the home team expects to win.

A ranking that rewards road wins is a hard place for a team that has played this many road games and won none. It is also the ranking that would reward an upset in Tempe or West Lafayette more than any other. Oakland has nothing to lose this week. That is a dangerous thing to be.
robert-morris:
Robert Morris is 1-3 and eighth in the Horizon, with a recent form of minus-6.6 points a game and no road credit to soften it. The Colonials went to Arkansas on Wednesday and lost 76-53, a road loss to an SEC team in a building that is very loud in November. On Sunday they came home and beat Capital, a non-Division I opponent, 94-45.

That is a team still getting its feet under it, and the Index's number is a reflection of a schedule that started in tough places more than a verdict on what the Colonials will become.

The scoring is spread wide. KJ Garris Jr., a sophomore guard, leads at 12.7 points a game in three appearances. Jalik Dunkley, a junior forward, adds 10.3 points and 4.0 rebounds. KC Ugwuakazi, a senior forward, is at 8.5 points and 4.2 rebounds. No one is carrying the load alone, which can be a strength and can be a puzzle, and early in a season it is usually some of both.

What the Colonials do not have yet is a game in which everything came together against a Division I opponent, the kind of night that tells a team, and the model, what it is capable of. The week offers two chances.

On Thursday Robert Morris goes to Toledo, a MAC team ranked third in that league's Index this week, in a road game that the formula would pay well for. On Sunday the Colonials meet New Mexico State on a neutral floor, a game that counts half on the road ledger but fully in the form number.

Garris is a sophomore who has already shown he will take the big shot. The question for the week is whether the rest of the roster can make the shots that come before it. A win in Toledo would make that question a lot more interesting.
iu-indy:
IU Indy is 3-1 and ninth in the Horizon, which looks strange until you remember what the Bricks Index is built to notice. None of the Jaguars' wins shows up on the road ledger. Their road game last week, at Morehead State on Saturday, ended in a 79-75 loss, close enough to touch but not close enough to count. With no road credit, the index is all recent form: minus-7.0 points a game.

The week's other result was a home win on Wednesday over Southern Indiana, 74-70, a four-point game against an in-state opponent. Two games, both decided by four points, one each way. That is a team living close to the margin, and in November the margin is where you learn things.

The roster has a sturdy shape. Gus Etchison, a senior guard, leads at 13.2 points and 3.0 assists. Behind him are two forwards with almost identical lines: Kameron Tinsley, a junior, at 12.8 points and 7.8 rebounds, and Manasseh Stackhouse, a sophomore, at 12.8 points and 7.0 rebounds. Two forwards pulling down nearly fifteen rebounds a game between them is a front line that can keep a team in games it has no business being in.

That is the case for optimism, and it is a decent one. A team that rebounds well can survive cold shooting nights, and cold shooting nights are most of what road games are made of.

The week offers both kinds of test. On Wednesday the Jaguars play at Penn State, a Big Ten team on its own floor, the kind of road game the formula pays the most for and expects the least from. On Sunday they meet Maryland Eastern Shore on a neutral floor.

The record says 3-1. The Index says ninth. The truth, as usual, is somewhere on the road, and that is exactly where the Jaguars are headed this week.
northern-kentucky:
Northern Kentucky has two road wins on its ledger and a three-game losing streak on its record, and the distance between those two facts is mostly a matter of when. The road wins came early: 84-76 over UTEP on a neutral floor on Nov. 2 and 102-94 at South Dakota on Nov. 4. They are fading now, worth 0.5 points a game together. Recent form, weighted toward the last three weeks, is minus-7.7. The total is minus-7.3, tenth in the Horizon.

Last week was a hard one, and there is no use pretending otherwise. On Tuesday the Norse went to Saint Louis and had one of those nights every team has once in a while, when nothing falls and the other side cannot miss. On Saturday they came home and lost to Central Michigan, 68-57. The losing streak is three. It will end.

When it does, it will very likely be because of a freshman. Willie Foster, a guard, is averaging 19.0 points a game over five games, the best of any freshman in the Horizon and one of the more remarkable early lines in the league. Noah Pagotto, a senior forward, adds 15.6 points and 6.6 rebounds. Eric Acker, a senior guard, is at 14.2 points and 5.2 assists, the playmaker who gets the ball to the people who need it.

Three players scoring fourteen or more a night is not a team that lacks for offense. What it needs is for the defense to hold up long enough for the offense to matter.

The week offers a breather. Berea, a non-Division I opponent, visits on Thursday, the only game on the card. It will not move the road ledger, but it is a chance to end the streak in front of the home crowd and give Foster a quieter night.

The South Dakota game showed what this team can do when the shots fall. The rest of November is about getting back there.
cleveland-state:
Cleveland State played three games in seven days last week, all of them away from home, and came home 2-1 with two road wins and enough close finishes to last a month. On Monday the Vikings went to Bowling Green and lost 95-79. On Friday they beat West Florida 69-67 on a neutral floor. On Sunday they won at Alabama A&M, 74-73. Two wins by a combined three points. Somewhere a cardiologist is updating a file.

The road wins are worth 0.9 points a game on the ledger, which is real credit. Recent form, though, is minus-10.2, built on the margins of a season's first two weeks in which the Vikings have had to scrap for everything. The total is minus-9.3, eleventh in the Horizon.

The scoring runs through one man. Rayvon Griffith, a senior guard, is averaging 17.8 points over five games, the steady number of a player his teammates look for when the clock gets short. Curtis Stinson Jr., a sophomore guard, adds 9.8 points and 4.0 rebounds. Jordan Lowery, another sophomore guard, is at 8.2 points and 2.4 assists.

A senior who scores and two sophomores learning beside him is a familiar shape in college basketball, and it tends to get better as the year goes on, because the sophomores learn and the senior gets more help.

The week brings a road trip and a homecoming. On Tuesday the Vikings play at Xavier, a Big East team on its own floor, the kind of road opponent the Index pays very well for. On Saturday Kent State comes to Cleveland, a short drive and an old regional rivalry.

The Vikings have already shown they will not go quietly at the end of a game. Two wins by a combined three points is either luck or nerve, and with a senior like Griffith, it is probably nerve.
detroit-mercy:
Detroit Mercy is 0-3, last in the Horizon, and still looking for the night when everything comes together. The Titans went to Xavier on Tuesday and ran into a Big East team on its home floor, the sort of evening a team survives and learns from. On Saturday they came home and lost to Toledo, 85-72. Recent form is minus-12.7 points a game, no road credit, and that is twelfth.

There is no point in pretending the start has been anything other than hard. There is also no point in reading too much into three games, two of them against teams the model rates above average.

What the box score shows is a team still finding its scorers. Tyler Spratt, a junior guard, leads at 8.3 points a game. Greg Grays Jr., a freshman guard, is right behind at 8.0. Ayden Carter, a senior guard, adds 6.3 points and 4.7 rebounds. No one is averaging double figures yet, which means the Titans have not found the player who takes over a game, or have not needed one long enough to find out who it is.

That is not a permanent condition. Rosters take shape over a season, and the player who leads a team in scoring in February is often not the one who led it in November. Grays, a freshman already playing a real role, is a name worth remembering.

The week is two road games. On Wednesday the Titans go to Eastern Michigan, a MAC team just down the road, a game that is winnable and would be worth real road credit. On Saturday they play at Michigan State, a Big Ten program in a building where few visitors leave happy.

The Eastern Michigan game is the one to circle. One road win would change the number and, more importantly, change the mood. Every team gets its first win sometime. The Titans would like it to be Wednesday.
